title: ParseSummaryV1
description: Everything a SQL parser can say about one candidate statement, with no policy applied. The retriever sidecar produces this with sqlglot; the Go guard reads it and decides. Splitting it this way keeps the parsing where the good parser is and the rejection decision where the runtime is — a summary is evidence, never a verdict. Absent optional fields mean the parser could not establish that fact, so a guard reading this must fail closed rather than assume a default.

ok.description: True when the input parsed. An unparseable generation is a routine result, not a service failure, so the sidecar answers 200 with ok false and the guard rejects deliberately.

dialect.description: Dialect the statement was parsed as. Must match the dialect of the database the plan will execute against; a summary parsed as the wrong dialect proves nothing about the right one.

statement_count.description: How many statements the input contained. Anything but 1 is a stacked query. Zero when ok is false.

node_kinds.description: Every distinct AST node type present, as the parser names them (sqlglot expression class names, e.g. Select, Join, Drop, Attach, Command). This is the input to the guard's ALLOWLIST: the guard accepts a statement only when every kind here is on its list, so a parser upgrade that introduces a new node type causes a rejection rather than a silent pass. Empty when ok is false.

tables.description: Every table the statement references, as resolved from the AST, lowercased and with common-table-expression aliases removed — a CTE name is not a table and a guard checking it against the schema would reject a legitimate query. Empty when ok is false.

functions.description: Every function the statement calls, lowercased. Needed because node_kinds cannot tell these apart: a parser renders a function it knows as its own node type (COUNT becomes Count) but every function it does not know as one shared node type, so pg_read_file, readfile and lo_import all arrive as the same kind. Without the names, a node-kind allowlist either bans all unknown functions or admits the file-reading ones. Empty when ok is false.

has_limit.description: Whether the input carried a LIMIT of its own, before any rewrite

limit_value.description: The LIMIT the input carried, when has_limit is true. Absent when the input had none, or when it had one the parser could not resolve to a constant — a LIMIT computed from an expression is not a bound the guard can trust.

normalized_sql.description: The statement re-rendered by the parser with the caller's row cap applied — injected when absent, clamped when larger. This is the mechanical rewrite only; whether to accept it is the guard's decision. Present whenever ok is true.

limit_injected.description: True when the rewrite added a LIMIT the input did not have

limit_clamped.description: True when the input's LIMIT exceeded the caller's cap and the rewrite lowered it

error.description: Why the parse failed, when ok is false. A classified, human-readable reason — never the offending SQL, and never a raw parser traceback, since both travel onward to a browser.
